** `momentum_health` was entirely absent from this bundle — no status, no MTUM/SPMO drawdown figures, no signals block — despite CLAUDE.md naming it as a required input to the regime step on *every* run, and this was precisely the week its answer mattered most. I had to infer the factor unwind by hand from `sector_relative_strength` (every AI-stack sector strongly positive on 3m and sharply negative on 1m while SPY was flat), which is a slower and less auditable read than the tool that already exists. Worse, the failure is silent: the fail-open convention treats a missing block as "unknown, no adjustment," which is indistinguishable in the pack from a genuine `unknown` verdict on live data — so on a `weekly_market` depth the gather can drop the block entirely and nothing surfaces it. The fix is small: have the gatherer emit `momentum_health` on every depth (weekly included) and, when it genuinely cannot compute, emit an explicit `{"status": "unavailable", "reason": ...}` stub so the pack distinguishes "the factor is fine" from "nobody looked."

** `momentum_health` came back **null** this run — the factor-unwind detector produced no reading in precisely the week it mattered most, with hyperscaler enablers −34.3%, design IP −20.6% and servers −18.7% over one month while SPY held flat. That is the textbook momentum-unwind signature the module exists to catch, and its silence means the validator's automatic risk-budget halving would *not* have fired had this been a trading depth. It should fail *loud* (log the reason and surface `status: unavailable` in the bundle) rather than fail silently to null. Secondary: `market_radar` gainers and losers came back as four all-null rows — expected on a Sunday with no session, but they should be omitted or labeled `no_session_data` rather than served as empty objects that look like a populated sweep. ** The deterministic trigger check fired on AMD purely because the *price* touched the parsed $500 level, but my published `would_buy_at` was a compound condition — *post-event* confirmation plus a 50-DMA reclaim, explicitly excluding a pre-event dip. The result is a full event-driven run spun up for a setup that was never actually live, five days before its own catalyst. The trigger parser could be materially sharper if it also parsed an *event/date gate* from the trigger text (e.g. "after 7/22-23") and suppressed or down-weighted the alert until that date passes, rather than firing on the price alone. That would save event-driven runs for triggers whose *conditions*, not just prices, are met — reducing exactly this kind of "premature trigger" cycle.

** Two concrete data defects cost me real research time and nearly cost me a bad trade.

`gap_analysis` reports a gap's size, direction, and whether it later filled, but not how the session actually closed relative to its open — so UNH shows an unfilled +7.4% gap while `pct_change_1d` is only +1.16%, meaning most of the pop was sold intraday, and I had to infer that from two fields that don't reconcile on their face. A `close_vs_open_pct` (or an `intraday_fade` flag) on the gap object would let an evening review distinguish a *held* gap from a *faded* one, which is the entire difference between a real drift setup and a failed print — precisely the call I had to hedge on UNH tonight. Secondary: `momentum_health` was absent from this bundle entirely (not even `unknown`), and `position_histories` was `skipped`, so two documented inputs to the regime read were silently missing rather than explicitly null.

The scanner should promote the top 1–2 non-focus setups (by swing_setup_score or upward-revision rank) into the focus set each run so they receive a chart + deep bundle, letting me deep-research them the same cycle they appear instead of waiting a week.

** Two process gaps cost research time today. First, candlestick charts did not render this run — `data/charts/` was empty even though the gather log said "rendering candlestick charts..."; the chart step appears to depend on the same blocked live yfinance feed rather than falling back to the relay bundle the way the rest of the pipeline does, so I judged entry geometry on numeric indicators alone with no visual confirmation of the actual price bars.
